title: PaxHub - OPS - Security - Agent Nexus Onboarding - ch-shared-cust-hub-logging-framework - Remediate Dependabot Vulnerabilities
description:
Given the ch-shared-cust-hub-logging-framework Git repository requires Agent Nexus onboarding and remediation of vulnerabilities reported by Dependabot
When onboarding and dependency remediation are completed
Then the repository is registered with Agent Nexus and reported vulnerabilities are remediated, mitigated, or covered by approved documented exceptions
And the shared logging framework and its consuming applications continue operating without remediation-related regressions

Context: Apply the security onboarding and remediation scope of reference User Story 3087639 to the different Git repository ch-shared-cust-hub-logging-framework. This story explicitly includes both Agent Nexus onboarding and Dependabot remediation; it is not limited to dependency updates. Inventory direct and transitive dependency findings, implement secure compatible updates or approved mitigations, and record approved exceptions with accountable owners and review dates. Confirm the actual repository registration and ongoing findings workflow in Agent Nexus. Because this repository is a shared logging framework, assess compatibility and release/version impacts for consuming applications. Validate changes in Stage through representative consumers and document production deployment planning and approvals, matching the reference scope; production deployment execution is not implicitly included. Reference: https://dev.azure.com/AmericanAirlines/PassengerDataHub/_workitems/edit/3087639.
acceptanceCriteria:
Register the logging framework repository with Agent Nexus
Given ch-shared-cust-hub-logging-framework requires security onboarding equivalent to reference story 3087639
When the approved Agent Nexus onboarding process is completed
Then the correct Git repository is registered and its initial security assessment completes successfully
And repository ownership, ongoing assessment configuration, and the workflow for reviewing and remediating future findings are verified and documented.

Remediate Dependabot findings with accountable exceptions
Given Dependabot reports vulnerable direct or transitive dependencies in ch-shared-cust-hub-logging-framework
When dependency updates, supported fixes, or approved mitigations are applied
Then every reported finding is resolved or has an approved documented exception, with no unapproved high-risk security gaps
And repeat dependency checks confirm the outcome and exceptions identify the rationale, approver, owner, and expiry or review date.

Handle onboarding failures and incompatible dependency updates safely
Given repository registration, security assessment, dependency resolution, or consumer validation can fail
When a required check fails or a patched dependency is incompatible
Then the failure is documented and assigned for resolution rather than treating onboarding or remediation as complete
And unsafe changes are not released, existing supported behavior can be restored, and diagnostics do not expose credentials or sensitive log data.

Update dependency configuration and release documentation
Given onboarding and remediation affect repository dependencies or security configuration
When the changes are prepared for release
Then applicable dependency manifests and lockfiles, Dependabot configuration, Agent Nexus registration references, and security/remediation documentation are updated
And release notes identify compatibility impacts, version changes, approved exceptions, and upgrade instructions for consuming applications.

Verify the framework and representative consumers in Stage
Given the remediated framework passes repository build and automated tests
When the updated framework is integrated with representative consuming applications and validated in Stage
Then existing logging behavior, log formats, sensitive-data handling, and consumer functionality remain compatible without remediation-related regressions
And deployment and test evidence confirms normal operation, with performance and reliability impacts assessed against the baseline.

Plan the production release after Stage validation
Given Stage validation is complete and Agent Nexus onboarding and Dependabot outcomes are evidenced
When production deployment planning is performed
Then the framework release and applicable consuming-application rollout plan, required approvals, schedule, and rollback steps are documented according to change management processes
And unresolved risks and approved exceptions are communicated before production release, consistent with the production-planning scope of reference story 3087639.
